description: Resource usage of NethServer 8 modules and of the containers running inside them.

panels.description: Modules known on the selected nodes, including modules whose containers are stopped but still occupy disk.
panels.title: Modules

panels.description: Running containers. A pod's infra container, which podman names `<pod id>-infra`, is counted too.
panels.title: Containers

panels.description: CPU cores consumed by all selected containers. 1.0 = one core fully busy.
panels.title: CPU

panels.description: Sum of container memory usage, page cache included.
panels.title: Memory

panels.description: Module disk usage: volumes, container images and state. Refreshed once a day, so figures can be up to a day old. A file hardlinked across two modules is charged to both, so this can exceed the space really occupied.
panels.title: Disk

panels.description: Processes killed by a container OOM killer over the selected time range.
panels.title: OOM kills

panels.description: One row per module and node. `core` is the core itself (redis, promtail, node_exporter, rclone-gateway, the shared rootfull image store and the `cluster`, `node` and `api-server` state trees); `unknown` is a container whose owner could not be determined, which happens while a container is exiting, when one was started by hand outside a unit, or when a rootless container belongs to a local account that is not a module. A module with disk usage but no containers is stopped.
panels.title: Modules

panels.description: Receive plots upwards, transmit downwards. Traffic of containers that have their own network namespace; a `--network=host` container's traffic is in the node's own `node_network_*` metrics instead. A pod is counted once, so this sum does not multiply a pod's traffic by its container count. Loopback is excluded.
panels.title: Network by module

panels.description: Container names are unique per module, not per node: `traefik` exists under both `traefik1` and `loki1`. Always read the module together with the container. Uptime counts from podman's own creation timestamp; NS8 units start containers with `--replace`, so a container is recreated on every restart and its creation time is also its start time. Disk I/O is missing for a rootless module until its user manager has restarted once after the core update.
panels.title: Containers

panels.description: Reads plot upwards, writes downwards. Rootfull modules report block I/O immediately; a rootless module reports it only after its user manager has restarted once, so an absent series here is not zero traffic.
panels.title: Block I/O by container

panels.description: Receive plots upwards, transmit downwards. Only containers with their own network namespace appear here. Most NS8 containers run with `--network=host`, so their traffic is in the node's own `node_network_*` metrics instead. Every container in a pod reads the same interface counters, so a pod's traffic is reported once against its infra container (`<pod id>-infra`) and the other pod members carry no network series at all. Loopback is excluded: `lo` is a container talking to itself, and it is large enough to hide everything else.
panels.title: Network by container

panels.description: Volumes, container images and module state are three non-overlapping buckets. Rootfull modules share one overlay image store that cannot be split per module, so it is charged once to `core` and they show no image usage of their own. The image walk stays on one filesystem, like `du -sx`, while the volume and state walks cross mounts. Hardlinks are deduped per module, so a file hardlinked across two modules is charged to both and a sum over modules can exceed the space really occupied. Refreshed once a day.
panels.title: Disk usage by module

panels.description: Volume metrics are refreshed once a day, so a trend needs weeks of range: this panel keeps its own 14-day window whatever the dashboard range is. Steps are the daily collection passes, not real jumps at that instant.
panels.title: Disk usage growth

panels.description: Volume names are unique per module, not per node: `openldap1` and `samba1` both own a volume named `data`. Size is the space actually occupied on disk and matches `du -s -B1`; a zero is a real measurement of an empty volume. Refreshed once a day.
panels.title: Volumes

panels.description: Time since the last successful container collection. The collector runs every 60 seconds.
panels.title: Container metrics age

panels.description: Containers the last pass could not read. Normal while a container is starting or exiting.
panels.title: Skipped containers

panels.description: Duration of the last container collection pass.
panels.title: Container collection time

panels.description: Time since the last successful volume collection. The collector runs once a day, plus up to an hour of jitter, so a value below 25h is normal. The textfile stays in place when the collector fails, so the disk figures go stale rather than disappearing: this is the only signal that they did.
panels.title: Volume metrics age

panels.description: Modules whose disk usage the last pass could not fully measure. A tree that cannot be walked is left out of that module's figures, absent rather than stale, while the module's other buckets are still reported.
panels.title: Skipped modules

panels.description: Duration of the last volume collection pass. It walks every module tree, so seconds are expected; a pass stretching toward the daily interval means the walk can no longer keep up.
panels.title: Volume collection time
